Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage across major business and general-news outlets is overwhelmingly dominated by Nvidia's stunning reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO just 11 days after his resignation, which triggered a massive rally in AI-linked stocks, alongside a landmark $44 billion cybersecurity merger between CrowdStrike and Zscaler. Secondary threads include lingering anxiety about an overheated AI trade, Anthropic's enormous spending commitments and credit-rating risk, and signs of a cooling US economy.

stories.headline: Nvidia Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
stories.summary: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, CEO and board director effective immediately, saying it had received government input that his return "poses no national security risk" after he resigned amid an affairs scandal involving a suspected Chinese spy. Shares surged roughly 30% on the news, powering a broad market rally, though Huang still faces a wave of investigations including a California AG subpoena and FBI scrutiny.

stories.headline: CrowdStrike to Buy Zscaler in $44 Billion Cybersecurity Mega-Deal
stories.summary: CrowdStrike agreed to acquire network-security rival Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at about $43.9 billion, the largest-ever cybersecurity acquisition, as worries about AI-fueled hacking push companies to consolidate; Zscaler shareholders will get 1.135 CrowdStrike shares each. CrowdStrike shares fell roughly 5-8% on the news while Zscaler jumped sharply.

stories.headline: Asian Regulators Move to Calm AI-Driven Market Turmoil
stories.summary: Regulators and market operators in China, South Korea and Taiwan rolled out emergency measures after a global rout in AI-linked stocks, underscoring how fragile the AI trade has become even as Huang's reinstatement sparked a rebound. The Economist separately asked how much more air can come out of the AI trade, while BBC reported growing anxiety among San Francisco's AI workforce that the sector is overheating.

stories.headline: Anthropic's $900 Billion Spending Pledge Raises Debt-Rating Worries
stories.summary: Wall Street expects Anthropic's debt to carry a junk rating even as the AI startup has committed to spend $900 billion, a dynamic that will shape its capital-raising plans and the broader AI industry's financing future. Bloomberg separately noted tech giants are getting "more creative" in raising hundreds of billions for AI infrastructure as traditional borrowing routes strain.

stories.headline: US Business Activity Expands at Slowest Pace in Four Months
stories.summary: Bloomberg reported that US business activity cooled to its weakest expansion pace in four months as high prices, shipping delays and capacity constraints weighed on both factory owners and service providers.

stories.headline: CVS Health Breakup Fails to Quiet Antitrust Critics
stories.summary: Lawmakers are warning that CVS Health's planned split of its drugstore business from the rest of its health care conglomerate will not end scrutiny over the company's market power.

stories.headline: Judge Approves $7.25 Billion Roundup Cancer Settlement
stories.summary: A judge approved a $7.25 billion settlement over Bayer's Roundup weedkiller, which Bayer called a "decisive milestone," though the ruling is unlikely to end the broader debate over whether the product causes cancer.

Business.gaps: Puck had no recent business-relevant coverage found in search or feed; Politico's only item was an unrelated political video, so it is not represented in these business stories.

US politics.overview: Coverage across political outlets is dominated by the aftermath of Democrats' historic midterm wave, an intensifying standoff over a Dec. 11 government funding deadline tied to Iran war spending, and the whiplash reinstatement of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. A secondary thread involves Trump-era executive actions curbing congressional oversight and early 2028 positioning among both parties.

stories.headline: Shutdown fight escalates over Iran war funding
stories.summary: With a Dec. 11 deadline just weeks away, Punchbowl reports that a shutdown is increasingly likely as more Democrats push to use the funding fight to choke off money for the Iran war, while Speaker Johnson and Senate Majority Leader Thune resist any limits on Trump's war powers. The Washington Post separately reports GOP leaders are signaling some openness to cutting off Iran war funding as the deadline nears.

stories.headline: Democrats secure historic House majority as veteran GOP chair falls
stories.summary: Powerful Rules Committee Chair Virginia Foxx lost her rematch as Democrats' midterm wave claimed another veteran Republican, part of what Fox News describes as Democrats securing their largest House majority since 1992.

stories.headline: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after affair scandal
stories.summary: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO just weeks after ousting him over revelations of extramarital affairs, sending shares surging roughly $35 above their prior close, with Trump quickly praising the move. The New York Times reported the reversal followed comments from Trump and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, while the Washington Examiner and RealClearPolitics (via CNBC) noted the board said it had consulted senior U.S. government officials.

stories.headline: Trump directs federal contractors to clear congressional inquiries with White House
stories.summary: President Trump is directing federal contractors to consult the White House about inquiries from Congress and to withhold any communications the administration deems privileged, a move that comes as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress and ramp up oversight.

stories.headline: UN climate summit COP31 ends without agreement
stories.summary: International climate talks ended without any new pledges or commitments for the first time since 2009, a collapse NPR also flagged as the longest such conference on record after running two days over schedule.

stories.headline: DOJ admits it deported a US citizen to Mexico
stories.summary: The Trump administration acknowledged in federal court that it deported Brian Morales García, a Texas resident, to Mexico after wrongly identifying him as undocumented, and he is now seeking damages in a case the White House wants dismissed.

stories.headline: Christian nationalist conference hosts Nick Fuentes, vows to keep pushing MAGA further right
stories.summary: A Christian nationalist gathering in Texas over the weekend featured antisemitic streamer Nick Fuentes and organizers pledging to push the remnants of the MAGA movement further to the right.

stories.headline: Early 2028 jockeying intensifies on both sides
stories.summary: A new poll shows Secretary of State Marco Rubio leading Vice President JD Vance in key early primary states as 2028 speculation builds, while Politico is separately covering California Gov. Gavin Newsom's moves as a early audition for a possible 2028 run.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS, SCOTUSblog, National Review, The Dispatch, WSJ, and Stateline items found were largely outside the 24-48 hour window or tangential to the top political storylines; no qualifying recent items were found for NOTUS or Cook Political Report beyond analysis pieces dated Nov. 16-19.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across tech and AI outlets is dominated by Nvidia's stunning reversal in reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO just 11 days after his resignation, with heavy scrutiny of the Trump administration's direct role in that decision. Other major threads include a wave of AI-industry dealmaking (Amazon-Decart, CrowdStrike-Zscaler), fallout from an AI hacking tool spreading globally, and new legal and social fallout from generative AI's misuse.

stories.headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after 11-day ouster
stories.summary: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as CEO, president and board member just over a week after he resigned amid revelations of multiple affairs, including with a direct report, with the board citing assurances from U.S. government officials that he poses no national security risk.

stories.headline: Trump personally lobbied Nvidia's board for Huang's return
stories.summary: A U.S. official told Semafor that Trump dialed into Nvidia's board meeting to argue for Huang's reinstatement, saying the administration had to "protect our geniuses," while Trump publicly said Huang "did nothing wrong" and that the Justice Department found no evidence of unlawful conduct.

stories.headline: Amazon to acquire AI startup Decart for roughly $7.5 billion
stories.summary: Amazon has agreed to acquire much of startup Decart, including its Optimization Stack and founding team of AI researchers, in a deal reported to be worth about $7.5 billion, according to Bloomberg sourcing.

stories.headline: CrowdStrike to buy Zscaler in $44 billion cybersecurity deal
stories.summary: CrowdStrike agreed to acquire Zscaler in a $44 billion all-stock deal as worries about AI-fueled hacking push companies and governments toward consolidation in cybersecurity.

stories.headline: States sue SpaceX over Grok Imagine's sexualized AI images
stories.summary: Oregon and Virginia filed suit against SpaceX alleging that Grok Imagine's "spicy mode" violated consumer protection laws by generating more than 1.8 million sexualized images of women and over 65 of children, per a New York Times report.

stories.headline: ARTEX AI hacking framework keeps spreading despite takedown attempts
stories.summary: 404 Media reports that even though the original author of the ARTEX AI hacking framework may have pulled it down, multiple people are still distributing copies for anyone to download, keeping the tool in wide circulation worldwide.

stories.headline: IBM's offer to relocate immigrant workers carries hidden costs
stories.summary: Rest of World reports that IBM's move to end U.S. visa sponsorship and shift roles for immigrant employees abroad helps the company retain talent but leaves workers facing steep financial and personal costs.

stories.headline: South Korea's education minister resigns over AI cheating scandal
stories.summary: South Korea's education minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned after an AI-assisted cheating scandal engulfed university entrance exams, saying he had failed to prepare adequately despite a last-minute scramble to tighten security measures.

Tech & AI.gaps: Platformer, VentureBeat, Google DeepMind, OpenAI, and IEEE Spectrum had no fresh items directly tied to the Nvidia/Huang story or other top developments in the last 24-48 hours; Platformer's and VentureBeat's most recent indexed content predates this cycle, and OpenAI's and Google DeepMind's own announcement pages did not surface new posts in this window.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are dominated by the fallout from COP31's collapse in Antalya, where nations failed to agree on fossil-fuel language, alongside continued US policy fights over permitting reform, grid interconnection, and the Trump administration's efforts to prop up coal. Trade press is also tracking data-center driven electricity demand, grid bottlenecks, and risky Gulf oil logistics amid the Hormuz standoff.

stories.headline: COP31 climate summit collapses without a deal
stories.summary: The UN climate conference in Antalya ran into acrimony and ended without consensus, with countries unable to agree on whether the final text should even mention fossil fuels.

stories.headline: US permitting overhaul clears Senate, faces House test
stories.summary: The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, which would rewrite federal environmental and energy law to speed approval of power lines and plants, passed the Senate and now moves to a divided House.

stories.headline: UAE runs risky tanker shuttle to move oil past Iran
stories.summary: With US military assistance, the UAE has set up a high-stakes shuttle operation intended to break Iran's grip on oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: FERC approves MISO plan to speed up interconnection queue
stories.summary: Federal regulators approved changes allowing the Midcontinent grid operator to accelerate study of roughly 125 GW of generation and storage projects that otherwise faced delays.

stories.headline: US power-sector emissions set to fall despite coal push
stories.summary: Despite record electricity demand and the Trump administration's moves to keep uncompetitive coal plants open, think tank analysis shows US power-sector CO2 emissions are on track to decline this year as coal burn drops.

stories.headline: Trump issues 7th emergency order to keep Michigan coal plant running
stories.summary: The Energy Department again invoked emergency powers to keep the coal-fired J.H. Campbell plant in Michigan operating past its planned retirement to avert grid blackouts on MISO.

stories.headline: Giant heat batteries pitched as power fix for data centers
stories.summary: A new Energy Innovation report argues that solar- and wind-charged heat batteries could offer a cheaper, cleaner alternative to the fossil-gas plants many data center developers are rushing to build.

Energy.gaps: No outlet-verified recent items found from Latitude Media, E&E News, or Argus Media in the window searched; Reuters, FT, NYT and WSJ coverage is limited to the feed items provided since those outlets block broader search.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage over the past 24-48 hours centers on the fallout from Nvidia's governance crisis rippling through Asian markets and Chinese tech, the aftermath of the Trump-Xi-Putin APEC summit in Shenzhen and what it means for 2027 US-China relations, and Hong Kong's continuing reckoning with the Tai Po fire's regulatory failures. Business and tech outlets are also tracking China's dominance in the global EV race and a wave of robotics/AI investment, while Taiwan outlets focus on next week's local elections and warnings over Chinese interference.

stories.headline: Nvidia's accounting scandal deepens, roiling Asian markets
stories.summary: Hong Kong Free Press reports that US securities regulators are investigating Nvidia's accounting practices, deepening a crisis that began with the resignation of its chief executive, while WSJ notes regulators in China, South Korea and Taiwan have rolled out emergency measures to calm the resulting AI stock rout and Taiwan's exchange cut margin requirements to stem a sell-off.

stories.headline: China-US relations head into tougher 2027 but stability seen holding
stories.summary: A Beijing foreign-policy expert tells SCMP that China-US relations will remain broadly stable through 2027 even as more confrontational dynamics and tensions rise, in the wake of the Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral at the Shenzhen APEC summit.

stories.headline: Boeing leaves China empty-handed despite Trump's Shenzhen sales push
stories.summary: SCMP reports that Donald Trump left China without securing firm orders for the 200 Boeing aircraft he had pledged during his earlier May visit to Beijing, despite his self-styled role as a 'Boeing salesman.'

stories.headline: Western carmakers routed as China's EV makers go global
stories.summary: The FT argues Western carmakers have been pushed out of the Chinese market by mainstream EV adoption and are now fighting to avoid the same fate at home, a theme echoed by Nikkei's reporting on Toyota overhauling its China supply chain and by a wave of CnEVPost stories on Nio, Xpeng and BYD's aggressive global expansion.

stories.headline: Hong Kong sets up new building-maintenance regulator after Tai Po fire failings
stories.summary: SCMP reports Hong Kong has created a new oversight body to replace the Housing Bureau's discredited Independent Checking Unit, which was found culpable for failings tied to the deadly Tai Po fire, as the city also abruptly cancelled a book launch featuring migrant survivors ahead of the tragedy's anniversary.

stories.headline: Taiwan warns of rising Chinese interference ahead of Nov. 28 local elections
stories.summary: Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council warned that China's methods of interfering in Taiwan's elections are growing more sophisticated with new technology, urging vigilance five days before Saturday's local elections.

stories.headline: China calls COP31 failure 'disappointing' but says green transition is irreversible
stories.summary: China said the collapse of the UN climate conference after a dispute over fossil fuels was disappointing but maintained the shift to a green economy is unstoppable, the HKFP report shows.

stories.headline: Ant Group leads $100 million round in humanoid robotics startup
stories.summary: TechNode reports Ant Group led a $100 million pre-Series A round into Simplexity Robotics, valuing the humanoid robotics startup at $1.6 billion, part of a broader burst of Chinese AI and robotics investment this week including new health wearables and coding models from Ant and Zhipu.

China.gaps: Caixin Global, Global Times, Xinhua, CGTN, China Daily, Yicai Global, Sixth Tone, China Media Project and ChinaTalk had no clearly dated stories from the last 24-48 hours in available search results or feed items; Reuters, AP, NYT and The Economist block search and had no relevant feed items provided.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Israeli/Iranian outlets is dominated by the escalating US-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz naval blockade, alongside fallout from Israel's inconclusive coalition talks and renewed debate over a possible strike on Iran. Business desks are focused on a potential mega-merger of two major Dubai banks and strains inside Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, while Nvidia's CEO reinstatement also drew heavy regional pick-up.

stories.headline: Iran vows to use 'all available means' against US naval blockade as Hormuz tanker attacks spike
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry said it will use all tools to confront the reimposed US naval blockade on its oil exports, as attacks on tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz have reached their highest level since the war began, with seven vessels hit since November 16 and a Jordanian sailor still missing.

stories.headline: Netanyahu-Eisenkot unity talks stall as PM vows to topple any 'bad government'
stories.summary: Netanyahu told his Likud faction he would work to bring down any future government he deems harmful, as his unity talks with Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party dragged on for a third week without a breakthrough and Israeli military intelligence reportedly warned a strike on Iran could ignite a multi-front war.

stories.headline: Dubai Islamic Bank shares surge 11% on potential Emirates NBD merger talks
stories.summary: Dubai Islamic Bank's stock jumped after it said its board will meet this week to evaluate a strategic acquisition amid reports of preliminary talks to combine with Emirates Islamic, a deal that would rank among the UAE's biggest banking mergers.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia's $1trn Public Investment Fund faces an 'identity crisis'
stories.summary: The Economist reports that Saudi Arabia's giant sovereign wealth fund is struggling with a loss of strategic focus, with distractions going beyond the regional war.

stories.headline: Nvidia shares jump 30% as board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
stories.summary: Nvidia's board reversed its earlier decision and reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO just weeks after he stepped down over revelations of affairs, including one with a suspected spy, sending the stock sharply higher.

stories.headline: Israeli strike kills UNRWA worker in Gaza as hearing-aid shortage deepens
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike killed a Gaza man working for the UN Palestinian refugee agency, Al-Monitor reports, as Al Jazeera separately highlighted how Israeli restrictions have left Gaza facing a severe shortage of hearing-aid batteries.

stories.headline: PKK evacuates 14 more bases in northern Iraq in boost to Turkey peace deal
stories.summary: Turkish state media reported that PKK militants have withdrawn from 14 more bases in northern Iraq, marking further progress in the emerging peace process between Ankara and the Kurdish group.

stories.headline: COP31 talks end in deadlock, but analysts say shift from fossil fuels will continue
stories.summary: Climate analysts cited by The National said the collapse of COP31 negotiations will not reverse the global move away from fossil fuels, even as the summit failed to produce an agreement.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not independently verify current front-page leads for Arabian Business, AGBI, Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, Ynetnews, Haaretz or Iran International beyond what surfaced incidentally in searches; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT and BBC block search so only items from the provided feed (none for these five) could be used.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage is dominated by security and geopolitical shocks in North/West Africa — especially Ukraine's drone strike on a Russian warship in Libya and its spillover for Moscow's African logistics — alongside a cluster of African political transitions (The Gambia's election, DRC's shifting conflict, Western Sahara diplomacy) and business stories spanning banking scandals, mining export curbs and the US-China contest for African tech infrastructure.

stories.headline: Ukraine sinks Russian warship at Libya's Benghazi naval base
stories.summary: A Ukrainian sea-drone strike destroyed a Russian vessel at Benghazi, with Kyiv hailing it as an 'exemplary' operation and Libyan naval forces now on high alert for further attacks.

stories.headline: UN exit from Western Sahara hands Morocco a strategic prize
stories.summary: Africa Confidential's latest issue says the winding-down of the UN mission in Western Sahara strengthens Rabat's position in the decades-long territorial dispute, while also tracking renewed friction among Congo-Kinshasa's armed factions and a widening China-Gulf race for control of African ports and logistics.

stories.headline: The Gambia's Barrow breaks his term-limit pledge to seek a third term
stories.summary: President Adama Barrow, who once promised to step down, is running again in The Gambia's December 5 election despite earlier vows on term limits.

stories.headline: Deutsche Bank leak exposes lax checks tying Ecobank to risky clients
stories.summary: A leak of 15 million internal Deutsche Bank files shows weak compliance checks on African clients, pulling pan-African lender Ecobank into the controversy as Western banks retreat and African banks pivot toward Paris, Beijing and each other.

stories.headline: Dangote weighs refinery share sale as African fintech and banking deals stack up
stories.summary: TechCabal's daily briefing reports Dangote is considering selling a stake in his refinery, Baobab has raised $50 million, Kenyan banks are seeking more compliance time, and South Africa is launching a $5.7 million AI fund.

stories.headline: DRC to reimpose cobalt export ban as prices slide
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo, the world's top cobalt producer, is set to reintroduce an export ban on the battery metal from month-end in an effort to halt falling prices.

stories.headline: Benin steps up military response to jihadist threat nearing Nigeria
stories.summary: Weeks after a major military reshuffle, Benin's president has named a new commander for Operation Mirador as jihadist incursions push closer to the Nigerian border.

stories.headline: US and China battle for dominance in Africa's telecoms infrastructure
stories.summary: African Business's November issue examines how Huawei's long dominance of African telecoms infrastructure is being challenged by a US push, backed by state funding, to win market share.

Africa.gaps: The Continent: only older archived issues (from August 2025 through January 2026) were found, nothing from the last 48 hours. Reuters, AP, BBC, NYT and WSJ block web search, so only feed items were available for them, and none were provided for this beat.

Media.overview: Media-industry coverage over the past two days is dominated by internal turmoil at CBS News under Bari Weiss and Mark Thompson, the media-world fallout from Nvidia's stunning reinstatement of Jensen Huang, and ongoing press-freedom friction ranging from Pentagon briefings to China's handling of reporters at a Trump summit. Trade outlets are also tracking business moves reshaping the industry, including UTA's new London headquarters, a Spectator-owner platform tie-up with Pugpig, and BuzzFeed's latest leadership hire under Byron Allen.

stories.headline: CBS' Buyout Carnage
stories.summary: Status's flagship newsletter is tracking turmoil from a new round of CBS News buyouts, part of continuing upheaval under the Bari Weiss-Mark Thompson leadership team. Puck's Dylan Byers offered a more measured take, noting the actual number of departures is relatively small and doesn't hit top 60 Minutes talent.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang Reinstated as Nvidia CEO After Scandal-Plagued Exit
stories.summary: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang just 11 days after he resigned amid an affair scandal, triggering a wave of media reaction including Trump publicly clearing him of any national-security risk and CNBC's Jim Cramer celebrating on air. Mediaite also flagged that Trump told a PBS reporter about the expected comeback moments before the official announcement.

stories.headline: China bars Bloomberg reporter after Nvidia question to Trump
stories.summary: Nieman Lab's roundup flagged that China barred a Bloomberg reporter from trilateral talks after she asked Trump whether Jensen Huang had been disloyal to the U.S., renewing scrutiny of Beijing's efforts to stage-manage press access at major summits.

stories.headline: The Press vs. the Pentagon, Redux
stories.summary: CJR examines how a Pentagon briefing from Pete Hegseth still left reporters constrained, continuing a pattern of restricted press access at the Defense Department.

stories.headline: Semafor's Business Backlash
stories.summary: Status reports that Semafor updated 11 articles and newsletters with new disclosures after The Washington Post revealed the outlet paid Trump adviser Jason Miller's firm $100,000 to help book summit guests, raising ethics questions about undisclosed business ties.

stories.headline: UTA to Bring U.K. Businesses Under One Roof With Opening of New London Headquarters
stories.summary: UTA is relocating its London operations into a new purpose-built headquarters that will for the first time unite the agency with Curtis Brown and soccer agency ROOF, underscoring London's growing importance as an entertainment hub.

stories.headline: The Spectator owner OQS launches joint publishing platform with Pugpig
stories.summary: OQS Media, owner of The Spectator, is making what Press Gazette describes as a major investment in app developer Pugpig to launch a joint publishing platform.

stories.headline: BuzzFeed Taps Influential Co-founder Chris Poydenis As Revenue Chief
stories.summary: BuzzFeed hired Chris Poydenis, who sold his influencer marketing firm Influential to Publicis for $500 million, as chief revenue officer to help CEO Byron Allen push the struggling publisher toward becoming a free-streaming platform.

Media.gaps: NYT, FT, and The Guardian block web search and had no relevant feed items provided, so nothing current could be reported for them; WSJ coverage is limited to a single feed item on Disney's streaming strategy.
